nodes.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then the binarization of $g$ is in Chomsky normal form.
nodes.title: Binarization of a reduced grammar is in Chomsky normal form

nodes.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then every word generated by the binarization of $g$ is generated by $g$.
nodes.title: Binarization adds no words

nodes.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then the binarization of $g$ generates exactly the language of $g$.
nodes.title: Binarization preserves the language

nodes.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then no production of the binarization of $g$ has the empty word as output.
nodes.title: Binarization has no empty productions

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar with nonterminals $N$ and initial nonterminal $S$, and let $t_0, \dots, t_{k-1}$ be the list of terminals occurring in the production outputs of $g$. Encode each symbol of a production output of $g$ as a basic symbol in $N \sqcup \mathbb{N}$: a nonterminal $A$ as $A$, and a terminal $a$ as the least index $i$ with $t_i = a$. The binarized grammar of $g$ has as nonterminals the…
nodes.title: Binarization of a grammar

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $a_0, a_1, \dots$ be its list of terminals occurring in production outputs. For a list $\sigma$ of basic symbols (each a nonterminal of $g$ or a natural number, a terminal wrapper), the head $h(\sigma)$ is the following form over the nonterminals of the binarized grammar (basic symbols and chain nonterminals $\langle\tau\rangle$ for lists $\tau$ of basic symbols):…
nodes.title: Head of a binarized output

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be a context-free grammar and let $a_0, a_1, \dots$ be its list of terminals occurring in production outputs. A basic symbol is a nonterminal of $g$ or a natural number (a terminal wrapper); the nonterminals of the binarized grammar are the basic symbols together with a chain nonterminal $\langle\sigma\rangle$ for every list $\sigma$ of basic symbols. Decode a basic symbol as a symbol of $g$: a nonterminal…
nodes.title: Valuation of the binarized grammar by yields

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the fresh initial nonterminal of the fresh-start grammar of $g$ occurs in no production output of the fresh-start grammar.
nodes.title: The fresh start symbol occurs in no output

nodes.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is in Chomsky normal form and no production of $g$ has empty output, then the fresh-start grammar of $g$ is in Chomsky normal form.
nodes.title: Adding a fresh start symbol preserves Chomsky normal form

nodes.summary: If the empty word belongs to the language of a context-free grammar $g$, then the fresh-start grammar of $g$ generates exactly the language of $g$.
nodes.title: A fresh start symbol is harmless when the empty word is generated

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $G$, the grammar obtained from $G$ by adding a fresh initial nonterminal (with an empty production and copies of the productions of the old initial nonterminal) generates exactly $L(G) \cup \{\varepsilon\}$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$ and $\varepsilon$ is the empty word.
nodes.title: Language of the grammar with a fresh nullable start symbol

nodes.summary: Given a context-free grammar $G$ with nonterminals $N$ and initial nonterminal $S$, this is the grammar with nonterminals $N \cup \{S_0\}$ for a fresh symbol $S_0$, initial nonterminal $S_0$, and the following productions: every production of $G$; the empty production $S_0 \to \varepsilon$; and $S_0 \to \alpha$ for every production $S \to \alpha$ of $G$.
nodes.title: Grammar with a fresh nullable start symbol

nodes.summary: Every context-free language $L$ is generated by some context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form.
nodes.title: Chomsky normal form for context-free languages

nodes.summary: For every context-free grammar $G$ there is a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form that generates the same language as $G$.
nodes.title: Chomsky normal form theorem

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a context-free grammar with nonterminals $N$ and initial nonterminal $S$, and let $t_0, \dots, t_{k-1}$ be the list of terminals occurring in the production outputs of $G$. This map sends an element of $N \sqcup \mathbb{N}$ (a basic nonterminal of the binarized grammar) to a symbol of $G$: a nonterminal $A \in N$ goes to $A$, an index $i < k$ goes to the terminal $t_i$, and an index $i \ge k$ goes to the…
nodes.title: Decoding basic nonterminals of the binarized grammar

nodes.summary: For a context-free grammar $G$, the list of terminals occurring in the outputs of its productions: going through the productions of $G$ in a fixed but unspecified order, list the terminals of each output from left to right. A terminal may appear more than once.
nodes.title: Terminals of a grammar

nodes.summary: A grammar is in Chomsky normal form when every production has output either two nonterminals, a single terminal, or the empty word with the initial nonterminal on the left; and either the initial nonterminal occurs in no output (so an empty production cannot leak the empty word to other nonterminals) or there are no empty outputs at all.
nodes.title: Chomsky normal form

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a context-free grammar with nonterminals $N$, and let $t_0, \dots, t_{k-1}$ be the list of terminals occurring in the production outputs of $G$. This map sends a symbol of $G$ to an element of $N \sqcup \mathbb{N}$: a nonterminal $A$ goes to $A$, and a terminal $a$ goes to the least index $i$ with $t_i = a$, or to $k$ if $a$ does not occur in the list.
nodes.title: Encoding symbols as basic nonterminals of the binarized grammar

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
